runs.t: Caching trades storage and invalidation complexity for reduced recomputation or I/O. Replacement policies such as LRU, LFU and FIFO make different assumptions about future access.

Define cache key, value lifetime, capacity, replacement policy, consistency tolerance and eviction trigger. Measure hit rate and tail latency, not only average response time; design stampede protection when many requests miss simultaneously.
A product catalog can cache category lists for minutes while payment balances should use much stricter freshness rules. A versioned key can invalidate cached category results after updates.
LRU is not automatically optimal; bursty scans can pollute it. Caches can hide performance problems and return stale authorization data, so document consistency requirements carefully.
